turns.content: For Q_{a,b} with vertices (0,0),(b,0),(a,1),(0,1), characterize a lattice-boundary triangle of area 1/2. Relate its unit base on one horizontal side to its third vertex on the opposite side.
Let T(a,b) be the number of such tilings. Determine the boundary values T(a,0) and T(0,b).
For a,b>0, analyze the tile incident to the right boundary and show why removing it leads to the two predecessor cases T(a-1,b) and T(a,b-1).
Explain why those two cases are disjoint and exhaustive, yielding T(a,b)=T(a-1,b)+T(a,b-1).
For the original rectangle, use a path with seven bottom-boundary choices but only six top-boundary choices.
Use the boundary values and recurrence to obtain the binomial closed form for T(a,b), then specialize the formula to T(7,7).
Evaluate T(7,7) and report the number of tilings of WASH.
